title: Choose the visual world for the cliproxy panel
question: One world for every page (Overview, Accounts, API keys, Models, Usage, Settings). Keep the lead, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Shipping Forecast
options.lineage: Met Office synoptic charts and the BBC Shipping Forecast read-out
options.thesis: Quota and health read as a forecast: every account's weather now, and when it clears.
materials: chart-white ground with a sea-area blue shell
options.viewport: Sea-blue nav rail; a one-line forecast per account in fixed read-out order (window, use, reset, state); below it the Outlook: one row per account across the next 7 days with quota windows as rising curves, reset ticks and cooldowns as front marks; traffic and the needs-attention list underneath.
options.risk: If the chart vocabulary is overdone it turns into weather costume; it must stay a table-and-chart product with forecast grammar.

raised.raise: Every figure is tabular and column-aligned; grey exists only as ink hierarchy, never as decoration.
All quota bars and Outlook rows share one time scale and one 0-100% baseline, so accounts compare at a glance.
Selection gets one reserved colour that no state ever uses.
Accounts are a ranked roster: most urgent first, each with the same fixed fields.
One type family carries every size; hierarchy comes from scale and weight, not extra faces.

regions.label: forecast read-out, one line per account
Outlook: 7-day quota windows, resets, cooldown fronts

options.label: Line Status
options.lineage: London Underground line-status board and Vignelli/Beck diagrams
options.thesis: Each provider is a line with a service status; requests travel from endpoint to model to account.
options.viewport: Top bar with tabs; a status board listing each provider line with 'Good service / Minor delays / Suspended' and the accounts behind it; a routing diagram of endpoints, models and accounts as stations on coloured lines.
options.risk: The most familiar choice here: status pages dressed as transit are a known trope, and per-provider line colours fight provider brand colours.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: jet-age airline ticket wallets and carbon-copy coupons
options.thesis: Each account is a ticket in the wallet; its quota windows are coupons that get used, validated or voided.
options.viewport: Navy header band; the wallet: one coupon per account with fixed ruled fields (provider, plan, 5-hour and weekly coupons, reset, status stamp); disabled or expired accounts stay visible, stamped VOID.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: nothing disappears, it cancels, which suits accounts and cooldowns. Wins on state vocabulary, loses on audience identification.
options.risk: Paper details (perforations, stubs) creep into costume; it would need strict limits to stay a working table.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Usage as a black-and-white data field of bars and columns.
options.viewport: Request records as a dense barcode field with numeric margins.
options.case: No state colour, so warnings and failures cannot stand out; loses on both axes.
options.kept: Tabular, column-aligned figures; grey only as ink hierarchy.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Config as fixed terrain; the request's route in purple on top.
options.viewport: Routing drawn as a course over a terrain of providers.
options.case: The map is a metaphor the operator has to decode; loses on clarity and identification.
options.kept: One reserved colour for the active selection.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Each account's life cycle on fixed-scale plates.
options.viewport: Accounts as plates from connected to expired.
options.case: Lands in the cream-and-serif rut and slows scanning; loses on both axes.
options.kept: One shared scale and baseline for every comparison.
options.risk: Precious where it should be quick.

options.label: Character Catalog
options.thesis: Accounts as a ranked roster of mascots.
options.viewport: A grid of account cards ranked by use.
options.case: Cute where trust matters; loses on both axes.
options.kept: A ranked, finite roster with the same fixed fields per account.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Pixel display type over fine text columns.
options.case: Display type fights dense labels; loses on both axes.
options.kept: One family at many sizes as the whole type system.
options.risk: Novelty type on a working screen.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern admin dashboard (Linear, Vercel, Cloudflare dashboard), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar nav; stat cards for requests, failure rate, tokens and accounts; a traffic chart; an accounts table with status badges.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other admin panel by design.
